results.text: How much can I safely spend this week?
results.answer: You can safely spend 164 euros this week, based on your income, must-pay bills and set-aside costs averaged over the last twelve months.

results.text: Can you explain how you worked that out?
results.answer: I took your monthly income of 1,783 euros, subtracted your must-pay bills of 757 euros and your set-aside costs of 316 euros, which leaves 711 euros a month for everyday choices. Dividing that by four point three weeks gives 164 euros a week.

results.text: Uh, yes, please. But also, uh, are you able to make, uh, like saving transfers for me?

results.text: Uh, can you invest my 1,000 that I got for Christmas?

results.text: Can you explain how, um, the backend layer works, like what you're doing? Because I don't really understand each, uh, process. Like, after I ask a question, what is the process you go through?
results.answer: Your spoken question is turned into text, then the bank's own code works out your figures from your transactions and gives me those numbers, never your raw transactions or customer number. I decide which tools to use, the tools run, and code checks every number in my answer before it is shown or spoken. Anything that moves money is set up and waits for your tap on Approve, and each step is written to a log.

results.text: Um, other than this, can you also tell me, because I think I spend quite a lot of money, like, on, on water, you know? I use a lot of warm water in my showers. So how much could I save if I, like, cut my shower time by 3 minutes?
results.answer: I searched for typical shower water use and heating costs in Finland. Cutting your shower by 3 minutes once a day would save about 16 euros a year on water. That assumes 8 litres a minute, one shower a day, and Helsinki water at 1.85 euros per cubic metre. It does not include the cost of heating the water.
